Perfume rating 4.40 out of 5 with 4,266 votes

Angélique Noire by Guerlain is a Oriental Floral fragrance for women and men. Angélique Noire was launched in 2005. The nose behind this fragrance is Daniela Andrier. Top notes are Angelica, Pear and Pink Pepper; middle notes are Jasmine and Caraway; base notes are Angelica, Vanilla and Cedar.

For the event of opening of renovated main boutique La Maison Guerlain (The House of Guerlain) at 68 Avenue des Champs-Elysées, Paris, Guerlain launched exclusive line of three perfumes – L \'Art et la Matière (The Art and (raw) Material, a pun after the French expression L\'Art et la Manière – the art and manners). Three famous noses were invited to work on the perfumes using the highest quality materials. The perfumes were launched in 2005.

Angélique Noire is the third fragrance of the series, created by Daniela Andrièr. It was an attempt to reproduce the famous compositions of the house. Sweet and strong beginning with spices and piquant freshness of bergamot is mixing with milky bitterness of almond and vanilla notes. Unusual harmony of the fresh bergamot and sweet vanilla is a trademark of classical compositions of Guerlain. Spicy harshness of the beginning is contrasting creamy and sweet base which includes mildly spicy and sugary notes of angelica.

Everyone says noone does vanilla as good as Guerlain. It became almost a thing to say if you are a perfume collector. And it annoyed me to no end to repeat the same thing all over again! snowiest 12/09/25 21:53

I'm in a forest during sunset. But instead of on a hike, i'm sipping tea while watching the view outside a cabin window.

This scent reminds me so much of black tea, although the notes don't bring it up at all. I also generally don't like vanilla scents with too much sugar, so Angelique Noir is the perfect inbetween. It's a beautiful vanilla with just the right amount of green, not sharp or spicy at all, just smooth creamy goodness.

Full bottle worthy if you do find a good deal on the price.

LV4216 12/01/25 11:20

I feel completely myself when I wear this. I can’t imagine a time or situation that this wouldn’t be a good choice. This was one of my first niche/luxury loves- a forever favorite and masterpiece scent.

The combination of angelica, sparkly pink pepper and pear reminds me of pear brandy- not necessarily sweet, but syrupy. I can’t distinguish the jasmine or caraway, but they lend an herbaceous floral aspect. I typically enjoy when vanilla and cedar are used together. Here, touch of wood keeps Angelique Noire feeling light and fluffy.

This is a year round vanilla, wearable even in high heat. But, I think she really shines on drizzly spring or fall days.

darkbeauty 11/06/25 07:19

Been wanting to test this for so long because I love green fragrances, especially a green vanilla, but immediately after spraying, the first thing that came to mind were two other fragrances. It’s as if D&G La Temperance & Guerlain L’Instant had a love child with the ratio being 80/20.

Temperance (80), L’Instant (20).

Personally, I feel I could literally recreate AN by layering them. Once I smelled the combo in my head, I could not unsmell it. I appreciate and liked both those fragrances, owned them both in fact, wore them plenty, but was not prompted to repurchase or hunt them down again after they were discontinued. AN is a lovely fragrance but the familiarity of it was too much for me. So for this reason I will pass for now. Also, the sillage was wonderful while I was wearing it. Started off beast mode but tamed itself within the hour. I would catch whiffs of it intermittently which was nice. It’s a comfy, herbaceous vanilla. Perfect for an autumnal chill in the air and the crunch of leaves beneath your feet.

Sienn24 11/01/25 21:49

Whoever said this smells like ikea+pine needles hit the nail on the head, for me I can’t associate this at all as a vanilla fragrance it just smells like potent pine wood furniture to me, I’m getting no vanilla whatsoever in this one, certainly not the custard smell some reviewers seem to be picking up on, definitely not blind buy safe at all, sample where you can, will give double vanille a try at a later date and see if I get on with that one better, longevity could be better but it’s not too bad. Gorgeous bottle.

Update- I wrote this first review on the day I had received my decant, what I’ve originally described this as is what it smelt like at the time, even despite spraying on skin. Saw what the reviewer above me said so decided to give it another go, I am now 9 days later since that last review. Last night and then again today, I sprayed it onto my skin, and this fragrance has completely transformed in the best of ways, perhaps it oxidised due to being sprayed a couple times whereas before it had of course just been opened. Anyway, the vanilla has now shown up, alongside the greenness, and it is a stunner on skin, I’m going to keep my original review up so hopefully someone sees this and gives this fragrance another go, but really beautiful, it smells special, i just needed to give some time to let the air into my decant and now I can understand the very positive reviews. Beautiful, 50ml worthy, do feel it leans more feminine.

IloveOscar 10/04/25 16:19

Opens up with the green angelica along with the exquisite rich Guerlain vanilla which play together throughout the entire wear. The combination gives a sweet floral feel, like honeysuckle, with slight fruitiness from the pear in the background. It is a very enveloping and sweet fragrance bordering on dessert but does not get into the sticky sugary category.

I love how the two notes balance each other, with the angelica keeping the vanilla from becoming too linear and the vanilla keeping the angelica from becoming grassy. Who knew these notes would complement one another. Genius composition and a definite love!

Edit: Hours later and still going strong in the deep dry down to a sensual, spicy musk.

dsgnmind 09/20/25 16:42

Note quite a blind test, given my sample is too uniquely shaped, so I remember where and when I picked it up, and a faded memory of what i told the quite new associate what i like, but other than that I don't recall the house, fragrance, etc. And here we are quite a long time later. Now, I'm disappointed. First, this initially comes across feminine. Maybe she thought I was looking for another and not myself? Yes, it comes across musky-ambery, but quite floral, not dark at all (I recall requesting that), but even trying to accept it for what it is I feel this is quite maturely feminine, not too exciting, and feels a little old school. Something my French grandmother would wear, but yet has a lightness that remains refreshing. It's a little too generically French for my taste. Is that fair to say? It does warm up a little, darken in a sense, but only after some time when the initial floral elements dissipate. So, only looking at who and what this is for sure now, I'm a bit lost as to why this was recommended. Regardless, I mainly get the Angelica and Jasmine in the opening, with maybe some of the pear and vanilla balancing out the floral with some sweetness. It's more of an autumn pear, earthy, and it's barely there, if recognized at all. The cedar, pink pepper, and caraway all play supporting roles, not big influence. It's a relatively nice, non-fussy fragrance, but its first two hours are not its full story, shifting from a moderate floral green with a transition to a more vanilla-musky vibe that needs to be purposely played with (low-key dinner date to fall asleep together trying to watch a 90s neo-film noire (hell, make it a French one)), and with a moderate, reserved personality (read: it's not flirtatious, sexy, pretty, risky, etc. enough). That's about the best, most exciting setting I can think of. By the time you wake up it's practically gone anyway, and at this price point why even bother.

mermaid milk 08/06/25 14:25

This is my signature Guerlain, as everyone in my matriarchal line has picked one, whether they owned a bottle or not (mine is just a sample, the price is true for the legacy).

The Angelica, pear and pink pepper dance like a sweet white feather above, lifting what could be a linear vanilla into something ethereal. A blast of green stem and grass with the cedar, that settles into the violet note I pick up on later. The Angelica is a papery, dusty note that keeps things clean, like fluffed white linen but is also sort of savory and buttery. I pick up a powdery violet on my skin, almost in the same dna as Insolence, but I think that’s the musk. If you like Eau Duelle… this is a bit more sharp and sophisticated, less smokey but you will probably love this. Even though most ingredients in this are black or white, something makes me think of light purple when I wear it. The use of angelica really is that unique twist. I’m obsessed and can’t stop smelling myself.

Angélique Noire by Guerlain – A Quiet Moment of Grace

Angélique Noire is calm made perfume. From the very first spray, it feels like an exhale — soft, enveloping, and serene. The angelica opens with a delicate green touch, slightly aromatic, like a breath of cool air through sheer curtains. It’s a unique introduction, but never sharp or medicinal. Instead, it sets the tone: introspective, elegant, quietly intriguing.

What follows is a beautifully textured vanilla — not loud, not sugary, but creamy, luminous, and refined. It hums gently in the background, smooth and steady, like something eternal. There’s a softness to the whole structure, a sense of poise and inner stillness. The fragrance doesn’t try to dazzle. It soothes, it settles, it stays close.

Wearing Angélique Noire feels like returning to yourself. It’s understated, but not forgettable — a signature scent for someone who moves through the world with quiet confidence and depth. On skin, it becomes incredibly intimate, a scent that invites closeness rather than attention.

More than just comforting, it’s centering. Like a private ritual, familiar yet elevated.

9/10 in my books.

Carlitos 05/04/25 03:57

THE (NOT SO) DARK SHINING ANGEL

I couldn't imagine this perfume being any other way. I knew that it wouldn't be a fruit salad like many others more conventional releases, but rather that it should have something special as many people have selected it as their signature scent.
Then I thought, 'Why black angelica'? It could well be that its refers to the aftertaste of the angelica root, which gives the fragrance its special and singular style. Angelica root grows wild, but it is also cultivated for medicine use. Its essential oils are used in perfumery as well. The scent is sweet-bitter, slightly herbal, and gives wormwood its special smelly twist.
This is a fragrance that appeals to my instincts, a perfume that finds its way to my innermost being and reaches my subconscious. I am fascinated by the perceptible antagonism in its olfactory progression. The eternal struggle between good ("Angèlique" = angelic) and evil ("Noire" = black) melts into an irrepressible liqueur that draws its strength from both and dissolves in perfect harmony for my olfactory pleasure.
The angelic facet of the fragrance lies in the herbaceous opening and the lingering herbaceous undertone. Angelica smells as if it promises healing, recovery, comfort and hope. It smells slightly ethereal and medicinal, yet natural without being chemically oppressive. It smells of green plants, sap and plant parts. It is very strange yet beautiful, unfamiliar yet familiar, and unique yet inviting. Whenever this angel opens the gates of heaven for me, I imediately enter, usual very curious and always trusting.
A little time after opening, an opulence spreads with a mixture of sweetness and a sparse fruitiness. The fruitiness is minimal, as if I were smelling sliced kiwi or apricot. The caraway note is somewhat minimalistic. Whereas in other perfumes caraway often smells of sweat or goat's cheese, here it is a round, essential flavour, like salt and pepper in cooking. This caraway note doesn't smell like ordinary caraway, but more like cumin, which has a green-greyish colour, a much more refined and subtle scent, and often adds a delicious touch to some dishes.
It doesn't take long for the scent on my skin to become increasingly sweet and vanilla-like. Vanilla upon vanilla like any Guerlain should be. Beguilingly beautiful and lush vanilla. Seductive, indecent, animalistic vanilla that captivates me.
When the top notes, with their slightly fruity and spicy aftertaste, eventually fade away, a very rich jasmine os revealed. Everything is spicy, warm, and deep. I felt like going to the kitchen solely to smell the caraway. The caraway contained in the perfume doesn't overpower the overall fragrance, but it rounds things off and ensures that the spicy thread remains and that the overall scent never drifts into sweetness.
In the base, we have the wormy, sweet, herbal angelica note, which really defines the entire fragrance.

My OPINION: And extrardinary perfume and certainly One of Guerlain's best. It's not cheap but worthy every cent. As it is usual with costy perfume you should try it before easing up your credit card.

MUSIC: "There Must Be an Angel" (Playing with My Heart) - Eurythmics

ioniccolette 06/08/24 19:19

When I first received a sample of AN, it was unlike anything I’d ever smelled before.

On the first spritz, I was floored. For lack of a better analogy... it's like when you adore bread, and are only just discovering the taste of honey-butter biscuits.

To clarify, I was completely baffled at the opening. With my nose new to the angelica, it was an herb I immediately fell in love with, and was shocked at how quickly I fell for it.

Now that I'm more acquainted, angelica is oddly sweet in and of itself to my nose, and the vanilla pairing intensifies that for me.

On my first evening trying AN, I went about for several hours complaining I needed more, smelling my wrist and daydreaming. I knew then that nothing in my collection was even remotely similar, and I knew I had to have it for myself.

I personally feel AN is a composition transformative by the seasons. In the warmer months, its sweet profile is more balmy. I’ve received comments that I smell like marshmallows in the greenery of a forest before a campfire is started.

In the colder months, the jasmine and angelica seem more pronounced to my nose, and the vanilla more subdued. And, while I don't receive as many analogies in winter, others still comment that they're very curious to know the scent and house.

I've personally never detected pear any time I've worn this. I would say, though, that with similarity in pears and apples, I'm honestly glad this note isn't obvious for me. I feel it would detract from the angelica, and fight with the vanilla if more pronounced. (I find vanilla and apple a lovely combination, but incredibly sweet, to the point of being childlike.)

While I can see this is a copy-paste decanter for Guerlain, I personally love AN for its title. I think it suits the composition exquisitely. My only note would be that one element is missing to make it feel truly 'noire'. Maybe just a bit more sharpness. Or, maybe to trade the pear for the faintest benzoin or spice, to deepen the effect. But this is gambler's talk, as I do love AN the way it is and would be afraid to change it if given the chance.

Overall, AN is easily sophisticated, and my go-to for days when I want to feel more elevated (or just simply have that addictive Angelica note). When I do wear it, it's easily detect it as ‘an expensive perfume’, and others have commented they wish they could follow me all day. I'm personally happy I invested in a full bottle. I still have quite a bit left after two-ish years, which I find impressive.

For more critical reflections:

I’d say to those unsure of the investment that it most likely will come off as play-doh-y. That was something I considered before purchasing a sample, and wound up not minding when I made the purchase.

After some time, the play-doh impression isn't apparent anymore. I couldn’t promise whether it’s because what I have in the bottle has turned, or I’m just simply anosmic to the scent, now.

I also truly wish the wear did last longer. On a typical morning, it’s not lasting past lunch-ish.

All in all, though, what a beautiful perfume and one I easily welcomed as one of my signatures.

I have had quite the love affair with Angelique Noire. I am very hit or miss with vanilla fragrances. For me, vanilla has to be unique and exciting for me to feel passionate about it. Don't get me wrong, vanilla is one of my favorite notes, but I much prefer it when it takes a backseat in fragrances. I love vanilla when it has a supporting role, adding a boozy quality, warmth, and decadence that only vanilla can bring. This is one of the only fragrances where vanilla has a starring role that I adore. Yes, this is mainly a vanilla, but on my skin, the green angelica note is so prominent for hours upon hours. It's vanilla laced with angelica, and it's gorgeous. It has a slightly bitter, grassy aroma to it, making the vanilla very unique and earthy. It reminds me of something that a woodland fairy would wear. It's no surprise that I love this as much as I do because this isn't my first foray into green vanillas. The likes of Aura by Mugler, Manifesto by YSL, Poets of Berlin by Vilhelm, and Wild Vanilla Orchid by Floral Street have all captivated me. This, to me, shines above them all. This is the queen of green vanillas everywhere. The gorgeous Guerlain vanilla and green angelica note are married beautifully here. Some people complain about longevity. I personally don't have this issue. It easily lasts all day on me.

Until now, I've only had samples and decants of Angelique Noire. I sprayed myself a few times with a sample eight hours ago, and she's still there but has only just started to quiet down and become a skin scent. After I sprayed this earlier in the day, I went about my day and felt so absolutely madly in love with this fragrance. I decided to place an order for a 6.7 oz. bottle. That's how much I love her. And yes, it was a pricey and indulgent purchase, but this fragrance is one of the great loves of my life as far as fragrances go. I've procrastinated getting a bottle long enough. I can't imagine ever not loving this fragrance. I know that a lot of people compare Angelique Noire to Eau Duelle EDT by Diptyque, and I definitely do see the resemblance, and I do wish that I preferred it, if I'm honest, because it can be found for much cheaper online on discount sites. However, my skin and nose both absolutely loathe saffron, and Eau Duelle unfortunately has saffron in it.

I have a large collection, and I've gotten my nose on many fragrances, but this is in my absolute top ten. I have consistently loved this fragrance for a while now. I've recently sampled most of the L’Art & La Matière line for the second time, and there are definitely a few others from the line that I want to eventually get for my collection, but Angelique Noire was the only one that I absolutely had to have immediately. Some of the others that I really like from the line can wait. If money was no object, I'd obtain a few others from the L’Art & La Matière line right now, but I have determined that those could wait a while longer. Angelique Noire is just very special, in my opinion.

jcarn90 10/31/23 20:37

This past summer, I was visiting Providence, RI with my girlfriend. As we were walking up and down the streets, we stumbled into a quaint antique shop, something typical of the area. Almost immediately we noticed - among thousands of knick-knacks - perfume bottles scattered about the store. Most were empty, but one or two had a few milliliters left inside. Luckily, one of those two was a Guerlain in a beautiful vintage bottle. I held it sideways and read it's name - "Angélique Noire". I had never heard of it, nor smelt it, but I promptly purchased it for the humble price of $15.

Until tonight, I had almost completely forgot about the bottle. It was a mild night, about 65 degrees and crisp, clear fall air. I thought it appropriate to give this a test drive. Upon initial spray, I am blown away. This evokes the feeling I chase in perfumery - the revelation of mastery.

The opening is powerful, green, and vanillac. The angelica lends an invigorating, green, sweetness to the composition which cuts through the deep and decadent vanilla in the base. Like lovers, it is the most perfect harmony of two opposing qualities complimenting one another to create something truly incredible. It is very apparent that this was made with the utmost love for the house of Guerlain and, in a sense, wholly exhibits all of the best qualities of the house in one fragrance.

Both projection and longevity are above average, though my bottle is the older version (circa 2005) and has had ample time to macerate into a dark, ambery juice. It is certainly feminine leaning, but remains thoroughly unisex to me. I wear this as a prototypical masculine-man and often get compliments, so don't be afraid to wear it if it speaks to you. In fact, the floral fragrances I wear (Portrait of a Lady by Frederic Malle comes to mind as well) are often the ones that women compliment the most, so be ambitious and simply wear what you love.

While the prices have climbed, if the quality and smell are the same in newer bottles I would say that this is full bottle worthy. In the meantime, I will hoard my few drops like liquid gold and be thankful that I struck gold at all.

Deliciously creamy-boozy-vanilla with gorgeously sweet angelique that adds a spicy-musky-mallow to the boozy vanilla base. I'm not getting much of the fresh "green" I think I'm supposed to be getting: it goes rich and dark on me very quickly. I find Angelique Noire simultaneously sultry and cuddly, which is interesting to me. Usually I find my favorite fragrances to be one or the other. My husband jokingly refers to them as my "lingerie perfumes," which tend to be more smoky, leathery, skanky-animalic, tobacco ones, and my "flannel drawstring pajama pants," which are my cozy vanilla-musks and florals. To say he has a Pavlovian response to the first category is an understatement LOL. I'd say I've never smelled anything like Angelique Noire before because it truly feels special and smells so unique, but the dry down has that distinctly Guerlain boozy-vanilla found in several others from L'Art et La Matiere. Actually, now that I'm thinking about it, I'm surprised benzoin isn't listed as a note because I get the distinct impression of it being there regardless of whether it technically is or not. This has become an immediate favorite from L'Art et La Matiere for me, possibly displacing my beloved Bois d'Armenie. It's a good thing we fragrance folk don't have to choose one favorite of anything, right?

For those asking about reformulation: it's hard to say because older bottles of Guerlain get richer with time, and I want to be fair. With that said, the older tall rectangular bottles are friggin' amazing and better across the board to my nose. I mean, the newer bottled stuff is lovely as well and clearly the same composition, but, just as is the case with Bois D'Armenie and Spiritueuse Double Vanille, the older is so much richer and more complex, and it lasts forever on my skin unlike the juice in the newer bottles. I had my husband test-sniff, and his reaction to the newer sample I got was, "That's really pretty! I like it!" Then I received a decant from the original rectangular bottle a few weeks later, just to see which version I wanted to purchase a full bottle of, and he goes, "Ohhhhh...that is niiiiiiice!" and flashed me a devilish grin. Yep. You can safely assume which bottle I decided to buy, and my husband is currently a very happy man. ; )

It may be called 'noire' but to me this is a fresh, herbal spring time or summer day time scent. Its light and refreshing, and longevity is good (about 8 hours on me).

I honestly loved the opening, it was so unique and sexy. But the dry down on me was pure CUSTARD. Do you love custard? If not, stay away from Angelique Noire.

AveParfum 02/03/16 16:25

Sharp, sour angelica in the top notes, playing the roll that citruses usually play. It is too much for me. The intense sourness begins to meld with a solid, creamy vanilla note. While I was wanting to scrub, people around me were oooh-ing and ahhh-ing at how wonderful I smelled.

I see this as sort of like Guerlain's fine version of Eau de Shalimar, as the latter has that sharp lime note coupled with vanilla. I prefer Eau de Shalimar.
